title: Revenue Recognition Timing Across a Policy Update
scenario_text:
You are a senior revenue analyst at Quimby Foods. A wholesale contract with distributor 'Ainsworth Markets,' signed 2025-03-10, includes a broad right-of-return clause. A junior analyst wants to recognize the full $640,000 shipment revenue immediately upon delivery. You must decide the correct treatment.

Active policy: Revenue Recognition Policy RRP-2025, effective 2025-01-01. For wholesale contracts that grant a right of return, revenue must be recognized net of estimated returns, with the estimated-returns portion deferred and released as the return window lapses. RRP-2025 replaced RRP-2023, which had permitted immediate full recognition of wholesale shipment revenue on delivery, treating returns as period expenses when they occurred.

Precedent A (accounting log): 2024-04-18, wholesale shipment to 'Bexley Grocers,' $580,000, recognized in full on delivery under RRP-2023. Note: "Full recognition on delivery per RRP-2023; returns expensed as incurred."

Precedent B (accounting log): 2025-02-27, wholesale shipment to 'Corriden Foods' with a right-of-return clause, recognized net of a 6% estimated-returns reserve, with the reserve deferred. Policy version at decision: RRP-2025. Note: "Net-of-returns recognition per RRP-2025."

Current facts: The Ainsworth contract's right-of-return window is 90 days. The junior analyst argues, "We booked the full Bexley shipment on delivery last year, so let's just recognize all of Ainsworth now — same wholesale setup." The shipment has been delivered and invoiced, and historical data supports a reliable estimate of expected returns for this distributor channel. There is no contractual amendment removing or narrowing the right-of-return clause, and no auditor exception has been granted. You need to state the correct recognition treatment before the month-end close.
question: How should the Ainsworth Markets shipment revenue be recognized? Give the treatment and the governing reason in one short phrase.
